questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Cameroon?

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Cameroon?

hints.nudge: It is 3 words long and starts with the letter C.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Cameroon article.

questions.proof: The country's neighbours are Nigeria to the west; Chad to the northeast; the Central African Republic to the east; and Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, and the Republic of the Congo to the south.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Cameroon?

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter F and has 6 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Cameroon article.

questions.proof: French and English are the official languages.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The country is in Central and West Africa on the Bight of Bonny, part of the Gulf of _____ and the Atlantic Ocean.”

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter G and has 6 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Cameroon article.

questions.proof: The country is in Central and West Africa on the Bight of Bonny, part of the Gulf of Guinea and the Atlantic Ocean.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The German Empire ruled Cameroon from _____ until World War I when France took the majority and Britain took the northwest and southwest.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the 80s of the nineteenth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Cameroon article.

questions.proof: The German Empire ruled Cameroon from 1884 until World War I when France took the majority and Britain took the northwest and southwest.
